title: Juvenile charged after 16 Pride signs stolen, damaged in Morton Grove - NewsBreak
text: MORTON GROVE, Ill. ( WGN ) — A juvenile was arrested and charged after more than a dozen pride signs were stolen or damaged in Morton Grove. According to the Morton Grove Police Department (MGPD), a juvenile offender was identified and charged under a local ordinance Tuesday after they received reports of 16 Pride signs being damaged or stolen in the village. MGPD said two police reports were filed in the case. One filed on June 9 reported 12 Pride signs had been stolen or damaged, and another on June 10 reported four signs being stolen or damaged. The damaged or stolen signs were located near the intersections of Dempster Street and Menard Avenue, Dempster Street and Fernald Avenue, and Beckwith Road and Waukegan Road. After canvassing the area, police found surveillance video from local businesses, where they were able to identify two incidents when Pride signs were damaged or stolen. One incident happened on June 5 around 8:55 p.m. near Beckwith and Waukegan. Police said a male subject got out of his vehicle and removed the sign from where it was planted and returned to his vehicle before driving off with the Pride sign. The other incident happened on June 3 around 2:35 p.m. near Beckwith and Waukegan. Police said four teens on bicycles rode by the Pride signs, when one teen grabbed a sign and threw it on the ground before another teen ran it over with their bike. MGPD said they are still actively investigating the incidents and anyone with information can reach out to police at 847-470-5200.
